citations.quote: A genuine single family office arrangement, established to serve the investment needs of members of a single family, which is not being run as a business (i.e. not receiving any income, other than reimbursement of operating expenses from the family) or have the pursuit of profit as its business objective, should not in the ordinary course be considered as carrying on a business from a licensing perspective.
the activity is capable of making profit; and the activity was carried out for the purpose of making profit.

readings.distinction: The defensible alternatives are shared negation, narrow negation with an affirmative second alternative, and an elliptical disjunction of negative alternatives. Shared negation requires both indicators to be absent and is contextually preferable because the preceding discussion treats profit-making purpose as a business indicator. The irregular “or have” prevents certainty. Earlier conjunctive formulas express this same reading, not additional alternatives. Their explanation that separately negated conditions joined by “or” require both absences was incorrect: that result follows from negating the whole disjunction.

readings.distinction: Here “or” falls outside the first predicate's negation and introduces an affirmative profit objective. This repairs the prior proposal whose narrow-negation explanation conflicted with its negative-profit formula. A genuine arrangement with both additional income and a profit objective satisfies this reading. It is syntactically arguable with agreement repair, but contextually weaker than shared negation. It was already retained in the validated proposals and is not a newly omitted reading.

readings.distinction: This elliptical reconstruction makes either absence sufficient, even when the other indicator is present. It requires understanding a second negative, which is not expressly written; it does not follow from narrow negation alone. The reading preserves the substantive alternative in the invalid proposals while correcting their attachment explanation. It remains weaker than shared negation. vocabulary_concerns: The supplied income fact operationalizes being run as a business but cannot represent its distinction from the surrounding case-specific assessment, including occupation or duty, continuity, and capacity to make profit. The formulas are conditional on the supplied abstraction, not definitions of business status.

The supplied facts cannot encode the defeasible force of “should not in the ordinary course” or the separate statement of regulatory intent. Those qualifications remain in prose; a true antecedent does not establish the conclusion categorically.

The genuine-family fact bundles genuineness, single-family status, and investment-serving purpose. It cannot separately resolve family membership or organizational structure; Q1 and Q2 do not supply exhaustive definitions.

The facts do not distinguish the office's business objective from investment returns sought for family members, or resolve which receipts count as operating-expense reimbursement. Supplying their values requires judgment without altering the supplied definitions.

The source packet's broader licensing-trigger description is not the requested issue predicate. Regulated activity, carve-outs, and Hong Kong territorial scope cannot be inferred from these three facts.
